# Code review iteration

Reviewed the full source of `github.com/kamilsk/forward` at commit `cc457c8 2020-04-30`: all 20 Go files (`main.go`, `mod.go`, `internal/cmd`, `internal/kubernetes` with its `cli` and `api` providers and clients, tests, generated mocks skimmed for context), plus `go.mod`/`go.sum`, `Makefile`, `.travis.yml`, `.goreleaser.yml`, and `README.md`. Review angle: real defects first (correctness, security, concurrency, resource lifecycle), then idiomaticity against Go 1.26-era practice, then toolchain/CI/dependency currency. No previous review files existed in `.github/reviews/`, so all findings below are new.

Severity: **Crit** / **High** / **Med** / **Low** / **Nit**.
Class: `correctness` · `security` · `concurrency` · `perf` · `api` · `idiom` · `modern` · `test` · `build` · `docs`.

## 1. Ports above 32767 are rejected by the int16 parser

`internal/kubernetes/types.go:26-30`, `internal/kubernetes/types.go:53`

```go
value, err := strconv.ParseInt(port, 10, 16)
if err != nil {
    return nil, errors.Errorf("expected a valid 16-bit port number, obtained %s: %+v", port, err)
}
converted = append(converted, int16(value))
```

`ParseInt` with `bitSize=16` parses a **signed** int16, so any port in 32768–65535 fails with a range error. TCP ports are unsigned 16-bit values (0–65535), and the upper half is exactly where ephemeral local ports and many custom service ports live. `forward api 54321:8080` — a completely legitimate invocation for a port-forwarding tool — dies with "expected a valid 16-bit port number, obtained 54321". Half the valid input domain of the tool's single core feature is unusable. The root cause is the type choice `Port int16` at `types.go:53`, which then forces `Local`, `Remote`, and `Mapping` into the same signed trap.

**Fix.** Use `strconv.ParseUint(port, 10, 16)` and change `type Port uint16` (and thus `Local`/`Remote`). `Port.String` keeps working via `strconv.Itoa(int(port))` and negative values become unrepresentable. Add table tests for 65535, 32768, 0, and out-of-range values (see [[#7. Test suite covers trivia and stubs while core logic is untested]]).

## 2. Unauthenticated pprof and gops endpoints listen on all interfaces

`main.go:7`, `main.go:43-44`

```go
_ "net/http/pprof"
...
go func() { _ = agent.Listen(agent.Options{ShutdownCleanup: true}) }()
go func() { _ = http.ListenAndServe(":1234", nil) }()
```

Every run of this end-user CLI unconditionally starts two debug servers: a gops agent and an HTTP server on `:1234` — bound to **all interfaces** — serving `net/http/pprof` via `DefaultServeMux`. Anyone on the same network can pull heap and goroutine dumps (which may include cluster names, pod names, kubeconfig-derived strings) and trigger CPU profiling as a trivial DoS. There is no flag to disable it, the listen error is discarded, and the hardcoded port silently conflicts with anything else on 1234 — including a user trying to forward local port 1234, which this tool makes likely. Also, since Go 1.22 `http.ListenAndServe` without timeouts is flagged by linters for a reason; but here the endpoint should simply not exist by default.

**Fix.** Delete both listeners from the default path. If profiling is genuinely useful, gate it behind a hidden `--debug` flag that binds to `localhost:0`, logs the chosen address, and uses a dedicated `http.ServeMux` rather than the global one.

## 3. Fire-and-forget forwarding with sleep-based lifecycle management

`internal/cmd/root.go:100-107`, `main.go:30-42`

```go
go func() {
    if err := kubectl.Forward(pod, ports); err != nil { ... }
}()
time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
```

Each forward runs in an untracked goroutine; the only synchronization anywhere is two magic 50 ms sleeps (`root.go:107`, `main.go:36`). Consequences:

- When stdin reaches EOF (piped input, `< /dev/null`, closed terminal), the scanner loop at `root.go:28` exits, `Execute` returns, and `main` terminates **without** calling `cancel()` — the spawned `kubectl port-forward` children are orphaned and keep running. That is precisely the "`ps x | fgrep kubectl | xargs kill`" pain the README's motivation section promises to solve.
- On Ctrl-C the handler cancels the context, sleeps 50 ms, and calls `os.Exit(0)` from a goroutine (`main.go:35-41`). Nothing waits for the children to actually be reaped; on a loaded machine 50 ms is a guess, and `SIGTERM` is not handled at all, so `kill` leaves orphans too.
- A forward that dies (pod restart — the number-one reliability pain for `kubectl port-forward`) just prints an error and is gone. There is no retry or reconnect, despite the project describing itself as "reliable multiple port forwarding" (`README.md:3`).

**Fix.** Replace the hand-rolled signal goroutine with `signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)` (Go 1.16+). Track every forward in an `errgroup.Group` (or a `sync.WaitGroup`), block `main` on it instead of exiting on stdin EOF, and wrap each forward in a restart loop with backoff to actually deliver the "reliable" promise. Delete both sleeps.

## 4. 2020-era toolchain with dead CI, archived dependencies, Go 1.11

`go.mod:3`, `.travis.yml:1`, `.goreleaser.yml:7`, `Makefile:4`, `tools/tools.go:3`, `mod.go:1`, `README.md:69`

The repository is frozen in April 2020 across every axis; the practical effect today is that it has **no working CI, a dead build badge, a release config that modern goreleaser rejects, and four archived dependencies**. One consolidated migration outline:

- **CI.** `.travis.yml` targets travis-ci.org, which shut down in June 2021 — nothing has built this repo in years, and the README badge (`README.md:89-90`) points at a dead service. Migrate to GitHub Actions: a test matrix on the two latest Go releases, `golangci-lint`, `govulncheck`, plus `dependabot.yml` for actions and modules.
- **Module.** `go.mod` declares `go 1.11`; `Makefile` pins `GO_VERSIONS = 1.11 1.12 1.13 1.14` and forces `-mod=vendor` with a committed `vendor/` tree. Bump to a current directive (`go 1.26` era), re-tidy, and decide consciously whether vendoring still pays its way for a small CLI — for a public tool it usually does not.
- **Dependencies.** `github.com/pkg/errors` (archived Dec 2021) → stdlib `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)` / `errors.Is/As`. `github.com/golang/mock` (archived June 2023) → `go.uber.org/mock` — or drop mocks entirely; the `CLI` interface has one method and a five-line fake suffices. `gopkg.in/AlecAivazis/survey.v1` is the legacy v1 import path and the successor `AlecAivazis/survey` is itself archived → `github.com/charmbracelet/huh`. `spf13/cobra` v0.0.5 → v1.10.x (brings `RunE`, arg validators, completions that supersede the toolkit wrapper).
- **Code era markers.** `// +build` constraints without `//go:build` (`mod.go:1`, `tools/tools.go:3`) — `gofmt` has emitted the new form since Go 1.17; the `go1.12` guard in `mod.go` is dead since the minimum supported Go is far past 1.12. `io/ioutil` in tests is deprecated since 1.16 (`ioutil.Discard` → `io.Discard`). The `tools/tools.go` blank-import pattern is superseded by the `tool` directive in go.mod (Go 1.24).
- **Release.** `.goreleaser.yml` uses `replacements`, `brews[].github`, and `folder` — all removed in goreleaser v1/v2 schemas; the config fails validation on any current release. Regenerate with `version: 2`, `brews[].repository`, `directory`, and run it from a GitHub Actions release workflow instead of `curl -sL https://git.io/goreleaser | bash` (`.travis.yml:48` — git.io itself was deprecated in 2022).
- **Docs.** `README.md:69` instructs `go get -u github.com/kamilsk/forward`, which stopped installing binaries in Go 1.17; the current form is `go install github.com/kamilsk/forward@latest`.

**Fix.** Do the migration above as one modernization PR: bump the module directive, swap the four dead dependencies, replace Travis with GitHub Actions + dependabot + govulncheck, regenerate the goreleaser config, and update the README install/badge block.

## 5. Malformed CLI arguments crash the tool with a panic

`internal/cmd/root.go:55`, `internal/cmd/root.go:67`

```go
if kubernetes.Forwarding.MatchString(name) {
    panic("Please provide a pod name first")
}
...
panic(fmt.Sprintf("Please provide the %q pod's ports in format [local:]remote", entry[0]))
```

`forward 5432 postgresql` or `forward postgresql` greets the user with a Go panic and a full stack trace. Panics are for programmer invariants, not for input validation — this is the very first interaction an evaluating user has with the tool. It also bypasses cobra's error path, so usage help is never shown, and the exit status comes from the runtime rather than from `main`'s error branch at `main.go:48-51`.

**Fix.** Switch the command to `RunE`, make `handle` return `error`, and validate argument shape with cobra (`cobra.MinimumNArgs(2)` plus the existing grammar check). `main` already prints the error and exits 1; let it.

## 6. Interactive input splits on a single space only

`internal/cmd/root.go:26-39`

```go
args := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text()), " ")
```

The interactive loop tokenizes on exactly one space. Typing `postgresql  5432` (double space) yields `["postgresql", "", "5432"]` and a confusing "expected port forwarding in format [local:]remote, obtained " error; a tab separator produces one token and the "enter a short or full pod name" complaint. `strings.Fields` is the idiom and fixes both. Two adjacent issues in the same loop: `scanner.Err()` is never checked after the loop ends, and the interactive grammar silently supports only one pod per line while the argv path in `handle` supports multiple pods and the `--` separator — the two entry points accept different languages for no stated reason.

**Fix.** Use `strings.Fields(scanner.Text())`, check `scanner.Err()` after the loop, and route interactive lines through the same `handle` parser as argv so both modes share one grammar.

## 7. Test suite covers trivia and stubs while core logic is untested

`internal/kubernetes/types_test.go:1`, `internal/kubernetes/api/provider_test.go:34`, `internal/cmd` (no test files)

`types_test.go` contains a single `package` clause and nothing else — `NewMapping`, the densest parsing logic in the repo and the home of the int16 bug ([[#1. Ports above 32767 are rejected by the int16 parser]]), has zero tests, which is exactly why that bug survived. `internal/cmd` (argument grammar, pod refinement, the interactive loop) has no test file at all. Meanwhile `api/provider_test.go` spends 63 lines asserting that `panic("implement me")` panics, and `api/client/client_test.go` asserts that a constructor of an empty struct is not nil — coverage theater that inflates the metric the Travis/CodeClimate pipeline used to report.

**Fix.** Add a table test for `NewMapping` (single port, `local:remote`, 65535/32768 boundaries, duplicates, garbage). Extract the parsing in `handle` into a pure `func parse(args []string) ([]entry, error)` and test it directly. Delete the stub-panic and not-nil tests together with the code they decorate (see [[#8. Dead scaffolding in the API provider and CLI client]]).

## 8. Dead scaffolding in the API provider and CLI client

`internal/kubernetes/api/provider.go:15-22`, `internal/kubernetes/api/contract.go:4-5`, `internal/kubernetes/cli/client/client.go:17-22`

The entire `internal/kubernetes/api` tree is a 2019 placeholder: `API` is an **empty** interface (with a generated mock for it), `client` is an empty struct, and both provider methods are `panic("implement me")`. Nothing outside its own tests imports it, and it has not moved in six years. In the live path, `cli/client/client.go` declares

```go
mux sync.RWMutex
idx map[int]*exec.Cmd
```

— a mutex and a process index that no method ever touches (clearly the skeleton of the never-built restart feature). Storing `ctx` in the struct is the related smell: contexts should arrive per call (`Run(ctx, ...)`), which would also let each forward get its own cancellable lifetime instead of one global one — a prerequisite for the restart logic in [[#3. Fire-and-forget forwarding with sleep-based lifecycle management]].

**Fix.** Delete the `api` package tree and its mocks; git history preserves the sketch. Strip `mux`/`idx` from `client`, and change the `CLI` contract to `Run(ctx context.Context, stderr, stdout io.Writer, command string, args ...string) error`, threading the context from the caller.

## 9. Forward error message prints the pod list instead of the ports

`internal/cmd/root.go:101-104`

```go
if err := kubectl.Forward(pod, ports); err != nil {
    _, _ = fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr,
        "An error occurred while forwarding ports %+v for the pod %s: %+v\n",
        options, pod, err)
```

The format string promises "forwarding ports %+v" but the argument is `options` — the list of candidate pod names from `Find` — not `ports`. When a forward fails, the user is told the "ports" are a list of pods, which actively misleads during exactly the debugging moment the message exists for.

**Fix.** Pass `ports` instead of `options`. A `NewMapping` test plus a `%!` vet-style check would not catch this (types match); a one-line review fix is all it needs.
